title: Fundamentals of Solid-State Physics
scope: This course introduces the fundamental principles of solid-state physics that underpin the behavior of crystalline materials and modern semiconductor devices. It encompasses crystal structures, basic quantum and statistical concepts, electronic band theory, semiconductor physics, and the thermal, magnetic, and optical properties of solids, while emphasizing their relevance to contemporary electronic and optoelectronic technologies. The primary objective is to develop a clear understanding of the relationship between the atomic structure of solids and their physical properties, explain the quantum mechanical origin of electronic behavior in materials, introduce the principles governing charge transport in semiconductors, and establish the scientific foundation necessary for the study, analysis, and application of semiconductor materials and devices in advanced engineering and physics courses.
description: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the fundamental concepts of solid-state physics with a particular emphasis on semiconductor materials and their applications. It covers crystal structures and defects, the quantum and statistical principles governing electron behavior in solids, the origin of energy bands, and the electronic properties of metals, semiconductors, and insulators. The course further introduces carrier transport mechanisms, including drift, diffusion, and the Hall effect, before discussing the thermal, magnetic, and optical properties of solids. Throughout the course, the underlying physical principles are connected to modern semiconductor devices such as LEDs, solar cells, photodetectors, and sensors, providing students with the essential foundation required for advanced studies in materials science, condensed matter physics, and semiconductor technology.

title: ELECTRONIC DEVICES
scope: The course provides a comprehensive understanding of the characteristics, operation and limitations of semiconductor devices. This course starts with explanation on crystal structure, semiconductor materials, fundamentals of semiconductors. This course helps in developing the understanding about excess carriers in semiconductors and its application. In-depth study on ‘junctions’ prepares the students for even a detailed study on devices to be studied later like FET, BJT, MOSFET viz. commonly employed in Integrated Circuit (IC) technology. Concepts of optoelectronic diodes will also be discussed in this course.
description: (as per the Bulletin): Crystal structure and growth of semiconductor, electrical conduction in solids, Elementary quantum physics (Photoelectric effect, uncertainty principle, Schrodinger wave equation and tunneling), energy bands in solids, charge carriers in semiconductors, excess carriers in semiconductors, Fabrication of p-n junctions, equilibrium conditions, forward and reverse biased junctions, metal-semiconductor junctions Bipolar junction transistors, field effect transistors (JFET, HEMT, MOSFET), Special diodes (varactor diode, solar cell, LEDs, Tunnel diode and HBT).

title: Object Oriented Analysis and Design
scope: The course covers the object oriented analysis and design methodology, requirements-analysis using a use case model, use interaction models to capture the requirements and the design of the solution, in sufficient detail. The course will also cover topics like design patterns, implementation, testing, and architecture with respect to object oriented systems. After completion of the course the students will have good understanding of object oriented analysis and design using the unified process and will be able to apply the methodology to typical cases. The course aims at imparting a good understanding of the main UML models used in the use case driven unified process and their application to given problems.

scope.supporting_text: The course covers the object oriented analysis and design methodology, requirements-analysis using a use case model, use interaction models to capture the requirements and the design of the solution, in sufficient detail. title: SOFTWARE ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
scope: This course provides an ability to identify, formulate, and solve complex engineering problems by applying principles of engineering, science, and mathematics. This also develops an ability to function effectively in a team whose members together provide leadership, create a collaborative and inclusive environment, establish goals, plan tasks, and meet objectives. In addition, this course also facilitates an ability to develop and conduct appropriate experimentation, analyze and interpret data, and use engineering judgment to draw conclusions
description: Software engineering is a discipline that allows us to apply engineering and computer science con- cepts in the development and maintenance of reliable, usable, and dependable software. There are several areas to focus on within software engineering, such as requirement specification, de- sign, development, testing, maintenance and project management. Software development outside of the classroom is a very complex process, mostly because real-world software is much larger and more complex. The purpose of this course is to present software engineering as a body of knowledge. The course is designed to present software engineering concepts and principles in parallel with the software development life cycle.
makeup_policy: • Mid-Sem Exam has one make-up. This means, that a student can abstain herself/himself (on valid reasons) in this Test. This make up would be conducted immediately after regular mid-sem exam and would include complete syllabus. scope: This is the first of a two-part course that is a General Institute Requirement, for all students in the first year of any program. It is intended to equip students with core emotional, social and legal literacy for a healthy campus life. This includes conversations around gender, sexuality, mental health, understanding of boundaries and consent, prevention of sexual misconduct, promoting responsible digital behavior and building awareness against substance abuse.
